featured.headline: The Art of the War Scare: Tehran Between Escalation and Capitulation
featured.rationale: This represents the active phase of the "Transactional Stabilization" hub. Washington is applying maximum kinetic pressure (2nd carrier group) while simultaneously opening a diplomatic off-ramp (Geneva talks). The juxtaposition of 7,000 dead in domestic crackdowns with high-level nuclear negotiation reveals the cynical core of the new order: human rights are secondary to the strategic transaction.

sections.headline: The Crude Reality of 'Liberation'
sections.position_rationale: Illustrates the *completed* transaction. Iran is the pitch; Venezuela is the closed deal.
sections.rationale: The speed at which oil sanctions were waived following the intervention exposes the true objective. The contrast with Cuba's deepening energy crisis highlights the cost of being excluded from the transaction.

sections.headline: Dhaka’s Pivot: A New Client State in South Asia?
sections.position_rationale: Demonstrates the global application of the hub mechanism beyond oil—expanding to trade and supply chains.
sections.rationale: The shift from Indian to US cotton and the tariff cut is the critical geopolitical signal buried under the "democracy restoration" headlines. It fits the "Invoice" theme: stability is provided in exchange for commercial realignment.

sections.headline: In East Asia, Security Comes with a Surcharge
sections.position_rationale: Moves the narrative from client states to established allies, showing that even friends must pay the "stability tax."
sections.rationale: Takaichi's hawkish victory and Taiwan's tariff concessions show that US security guarantees now require reciprocal economic or military payment.

sections.headline: Revitalization or Rent-Seeking?
sections.position_rationale: Concludes the "Invoice" section with the transatlantic alliance adapting to the new reality.
sections.rationale: The "Arctic Sentry" mission in Greenland is a specific concession to Washington's territorial interests, dressed up as alliance revitalization.

quick_hits.content: 6,000 reported dead in three days as the world looks elsewhere.

quick_hits.headline: Navalny Poison Confirmed

quick_hits.headline: West Bank 'De Facto Annexation'

quick_hits.headline: US Repeals Climate Finding

narrative_arc: Washington shifts from kinetic disruption to commercial extraction, converting security crises in Iran and Venezuela into tangible assets while invoicing allies for continued protection.
narrative_arc_explanation: Captures the "Shock to Invoice" transition identified by the editor, linking the disparate regions through the logic of payment.

section_groups.title: The Hub: Maximum Pressure
section_groups.group_rationale: Establishes the active "pitch" phase of the transactional model—creating a crisis to sell a solution.

section_groups.title: The Invoice: Paying for Stability
section_groups.group_rationale: Case studies of the transaction completed—US intervention followed immediately by resource extraction or trade realignment.

section_groups.title: The Premium: Security Costs
section_groups.group_rationale: Shows how established alliances are being monetized under the new "pay-to-play" security architecture.

transitions.cluster_64 \u2192 cluster_19: [The coercive pressure currently being applied to Tehran has already achieved its objective in Caracas, where the focus has shifted from conflict to cash flow.]
transitions.cluster_19 \u2192 cluster_24: [While Washington secures energy assets in the Americas, it is using similar economic levers to secure political allegiance in South Asia.]
transitions.cluster_49 \u2192 cluster_56: [The realization that American security now comes with a surcharge is not limited to the Pacific; in Munich, European leaders are learning the new price of the transatlantic bond.]

hub_explanation: A shift from "hegemonic stability" (providing order as a public good) to "transactional order" (providing stability as a private service). Washington is liquidating its role as global policeman to become a global security contractor, where protection and stability are available only to those who pay in resources, trade concessions, or strategic compliance.
